$comment: A running synchronization was invisible: `synchronization.status` is null on every sync, no execution_trace is `running` mid-flight, and POST /synchronizations/{id}/run blocks for the whole run (74.6s measured for 12 objects x 6 files). This schema is the missing progress record. It is deliberately NOT synchronization_log: that one is built in memory, persisted once at the end, and is appendOnly+immutable, so it cannot be updated while a run is in flight. It is deliberately NOT execution_trace either: the trace GROWS with the run (one step per synchronised object; it once held a second copy of a 19,822-object import), and re-saving a growing object on every progress tick is exactly the cost this feature must not add. Every field here is a scalar, so the record stays CONSTANT SIZE however large the corpus is, and a throttled update is cheap.
$comment-registers: DECLARING THE SCHEMA IS NOT ATTACHING IT. `components.schemas` creates the schema; the register's own `schemas` list is what binds it to the `openconnector` register, and only a bound schema can be read through /apps/openregister/api/objects/openconnector/synchronization_run. Without this block the schema existed on the instance (so the seed's slug check passed) while the SynchronizationRuns index page still failed with `Error fetching openconnector-synchronization_run collection`. The merge concatenates lists, so this appends to the monolith's list rather than replacing it (ADR-037).

synchronization_run.title: Synchronization Run
synchronization_run.summary: Live progress of one synchronization run — written at start, updated on a time throttle, finalised at the end
synchronization_run.description: Small, mutable, constant-size. Created with status `running` before the first page is fetched so a run is observable WHILE it happens rather than only after it finishes, updated no more often than the engine's throttle allows, and finalised with a terminal status. Progress writes are best-effort: a failure to record progress must never fail the run it is describing, but the failures are counted in `progressWriteFailures` so a silently broken recorder cannot pass as a healthy one.

synchronizationId.description: The synchronization this run belongs to
synchronizationId.title: Synchronization

status.description: Live state of the run. `running` is written before any work starts.
status.title: Status

updatedAt.description: When progress was last recorded — the field that tells a live run from a stalled one
updatedAt.title: Updated At

finishedAt.description: When the run reached a terminal status
finishedAt.title: Finished At

found.description: Objects seen in the source so far
found.title: Found

processed.description: Objects processed so far — with `found`, this is the progress fraction
processed.title: Processed

invalid.description: Objects rejected as invalid so far
invalid.title: Invalid

currentPage.description: Page the fetch loop is on, so a long paginated crawl visibly advances
currentPage.title: Current Page

filesPending.description: Files queued but not yet fetched. Non-zero means a deletion sweep must NOT treat a missing file as absent from the source.
filesPending.title: Files Pending

progressWriteFailures.description: How many progress writes failed and were swallowed. A recorder that silently stopped working would otherwise look identical to a healthy one.
progressWriteFailures.title: Progress Write Failures

message.description: Terminal message, or the reason a run stopped early
message.title: Message

progressWrites.title: Progress Writes
progressWrites.description: How many progress writes this run issued. With progressWriteMillis this is the feature's own overhead, reported by every run rather than measured once on a bench.

progressWriteMillis.title: Progress Write Millis
progressWriteMillis.description: Total milliseconds spent inside progress writes. Divide by the run's executionTime for the exact overhead — differencing two whole runs cannot resolve a few percent on a loaded instance.
